L2 records reinforce the high direction: apixaban 34–88% and dog absolute F=88%, alpelisib complete in mice and 58% in rats, daridorexant absolute F=62%, AZD0837 ~22–55%, papaverine relative 54–68%, ONO-4641 monkey F=0.71, and qualitative good oral bioavailability for CPI-0610, brepocitinib, and MK-8628.

The only sub-threshold value, daridorexant rat F=9% at 10 mg/kg, is species-specific and is outweighed by human absolute F=62% and population PK F=0.41; it does not provide affirmative evidence that the query has F<20%.
Fasted-state evidence is supportive: vernakalant absolute F=58–71% in fasted volunteers and apixaban ~50% unaffected by food.

The query's physicochemical prior is favorable (MW 324, logD 1.29, TPSA 45.6, HBD 1, rotatable bonds 4), and the quinuclidine-quinoline secondary-alcohol scaffold is consistent with orally bioavailable cinchona alkaloids; strong basic pKa 9.28 and neutral fraction 0.01 leave permeability uncertainty but are not affirmative evidence for F<20%.

The new L5 gut-wall efflux/intestinal-metabolism records are for other molecules; the closest structural analog (compound 27, a methoxyquinoline basic amine) shows high Caco-2 permeability and no significant efflux (C66/C69/C73 are duplicate records of the same measurement), providing weak mechanistic support but no query-specific measurement.
